verses.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by God's will, in keeping with the promise of life in Christ Jesus,
to Timothy, my dear child: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
I thank God, whom I serve as my ancestors did with a clear conscience. Night and day, I remember you in my prayers.
I long to see you. I remember your tears, and I would be filled with joy.
I remember your sincere faith, which first lived in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and I'm convinced it lives in you too.
That's why I remind you to fan into flame the gift of God that is in you through the laying on of my hands.
God didn't give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
So don't be ashamed of the testimony about our Lord or of me, his prisoner. Instead, share in suffering for the Good News by God's power.
God saved us and called us to a holy calling—not because of what we did, but because of his own purpose and grace. He gave us this grace in Christ Jesus before time began,
and now he has revealed it through the appearing of our Savior, Christ Jesus. He broke the power of death and brought life and immortality to light through the Good News.
I was appointed to serve as its preacher, apostle, and teacher to the Gentiles.
That's why I suffer as I do. But I'm not ashamed, because I know the one I've trusted, and I'm convinced he can guard what I've entrusted to him until that day.
Hold on to the pattern of sound teaching you heard from me, with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
Guard the precious truth entrusted to you through the Holy Spirit who lives in us.
You know that everyone in Asia turned away from me, including Phygelus and Hermogenes.
May the Lord show mercy to Onesiphorus and his household. He often refreshed me and wasn't ashamed that I was in chains.
When he came to Rome, he searched hard for me and found me.
May the Lord grant him mercy from the Lord on that day. You know how much he helped me in Ephesus.
